picked.t: Widespread flooding disrupts traffic, business in Hanoi after heavy rain overnight
picked.body: Rainfall recorded from 7 p.m. Wednesday to 3 a.m. Thursday reached 199 mm in Tu Liem, 190 mm in Hai Ba Trung, 182 mm in Cau Giay, 164 mm in Yen So and 153 mm in Thanh Liet, according to the Hanoi Sewerage Company. Floodwaters of 30-50 centimeters covered numerous roads, while some low-lying areas were submerged by nearly a meter. Several major routes became difficult or impossible for vehicles to pass, leaving motorists stranded in long traffic queues and forcing others to seek higher ground. On some roads, water covered most of the street surface, with authorities restricting traffic in flooded sections. Vehicles were forced to move slowly through deep water, while some stalled and required assistance. The flooding was particularly severe in western and southwestern parts of the city, including Tay Mo and nearby areas. Some streets were submerged by 30-50 cm, while Cau Coc Street was covered by more than half a meter of water and nearly one meter in some sections. Flooding also disrupted public services and daily routines. Some schools closed or switched to online classes, while residents skipped work because of impassable roads. In several neighborhoods, people moved goods and vehicles to higher ground to protect them from rising water. The disruption extended to major traffic corridors across the city, with severe congestion reported as vehicles were diverted toward higher ground. Some commuters abandoned their vehicles or pushed stalled motorbikes through the water. Central areas experienced less severe flooding. Some streets had drained by around 8:40 a.m., while localized flooding in other areas cleared later in the morning. The Hanoi Construction Department said continuous rain since Sept. 14 had brought cumulative rainfall above 400 mm in many parts of the city and above 500 mm in several areas. The Nhue River and its tributaries were at alarm levels, while high downstream water levels restricted natural drainage. By 12:40 p.m., 36 pumping stations were operating at maximum capacity. Water levels were gradually receding in some flooded areas, including Phu Dien, Tu Liem and Nghia Do, where flooding had earlier reached 30-40 cm. However, low-lying areas of the Nhue River basin, particularly Tay Mo and Xuan Phuong, remained flooded. The National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting warned of thunderstorms in the following hours, with possible tornadoes, lightning, strong wind gusts and hail. The heavy rain was attributed to the interaction between a tropical depression and the intertropical convergence zone, which brought continuous rainfall to Hanoi from Sept. 14 to 17.

picked.t: Metro construction triggers 3-km traffic jam at HCMC airport gateway
picked.body: By 8 a.m., the traffic jam stretched for more than 3 km. The most severe gridlock centered around an intersection spanning from the Tham Luong Bridge to the Truong Chinh-Cong Hoa junction. The congestion resulted from partial road closures along routes paralleling Metro Line 2, or Ben Thanh - Tham Luong. Barricades went up this morning on Truong Chinh, Tan Ky Tan Quy, and Huynh Van Gam streets to accommodate the construction of the ST9 (Ba Queo) Station. Tan Son Nhat is Vietnam's busiest airport and sits near several major arterial roads, creating consistently heavy traffic in the area. Commuters typically surge from the An Suong area toward the city center in the mornings, with the traffic flow reversing in the afternoons. Construction workers helped regulate traffic around the Ba Queo Station construction site near the Truong Chinh–Cong Hoa intersection. Congestion stretched for about 3 km between Phan Van Bach and Truong Chinh streets. This section was one of the first areas barricaded for the construction of Metro Line 2, which will link the city center to its northwestern gateway. Traffic backed up alongside the metro construction barriers, where authorities installed numerous signs to guide motorists. To ease the gridlock, the city urged commuters traveling from An Suong toward the downtown area to take alternative routes. 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남 노동계에서 민간 부문의 주당 근로시간을 40시간으로 줄여야 목소리가 커지고 있는 가운데 베트남 정부는 근로시간 단축이 시기상조라는 입장을 분명히 밝혔다. 생산성 개선이 선행되지 않은 상태에서 근로시간을 줄이면 인건비가 오르고 경제 성장에도 부담이 될 수 있다는 우려에서다. 베트남 내무부는 다낭시 지역사회의 노동법 개정을 통한 주당 근로시간을 현행 48시간에서 40~44시간으로 줄여야 한다는 의견에 이 같이 답변했다. 앞서 다낭시 유권자들은 “근무시간 단축은 근로자들에게 휴식과 회복, 가족 돌봄을 위한 더 많은 시간을 부여해 삶의 질을 높임과 동시에 다른 국가들의 노동 환경 추세에 더욱 가깝게 만들 것”이라며 근로시간 단축을 요구한 바 있다. 그러나 내무부는 “이러한 변화는 근로자뿐만 아니라 사용자, 기업 운영, 노동 시장, 생산성, 나아가 경제 전반에 광범위한 영향을 미칠 것”이라며 “현재 베트남의 노동 생산성은 역내 다른 여러 국가들에 비해 여전히 낮은 수준으로, 생산성 향상 없이 근로시간만 단축할 경우, 인건비 상승과, 기업 경쟁력 약화, 근로자 소득 감소, 고용에 미치는 부정적 영향 등이 초래될 수 있다”고 반대의사를 분명히 밝혔다. 내무부는 이어 “향후 몇 년간 두 자릿수 성장 목표를 포함해 더 강한 경제성장을 추진하고 있어, 근로시간 규정 변경은 신중한 검토가 필요한 정책”이라며 현행 주 48시간 상한을 유지하되, 가능한 기업부터 주 40시간제를 계속 권장하는 방향을 내무부는 제안했다. 현행 노동법상 법정 근로시간은 일 8시간, 주 48시간을 초과할 수 없도록 규정하고 있으며, 기업들이 자발적으로 주 40시간 근무제를 도입하도록 권장하고 있다. 최근 베트남에서는 민간 부문의 근로시간 단축을 요구하는 목소리가 커지고 있다. 앞서 북부 선라성(Sơn La) 내무국은 민간부문 근무시간을 공공부문과 맞추기 위해 주 40~44시간으로 단계적으로 줄이자고 건의했지만, 내무부는 이를 거부한 바 있다. 베트남노동총연맹 역시 지난 6월 제 14차 총회에서 이와 유사한 건의를 한 바 있다. 한편, 베트남은 1999년부터 공무원, 공공기관 종사자를 비롯한 공공 부문 근로자에게 주 40시간 근무제를 적용해오고 있다.

picked.t: Central Ho Chi Minh City streets to go one-way for 3 years for metro construction
picked.body: Under a plan recently agreed on by the city Department of Construction, construction of Tao Dan Station (ST2) on Metro Line 2, or Ben Thanh-Tham Luong, will be carried out in five phases over more than three years. Contractors will gradually fence off construction areas, build temporary roads and adjust traffic flows on several surrounding streets. On Cach Mang Thang Tam, a 350-meter section will be converted to one-way traffic from Nguyen Du toward Nguyen Thi Minh Khai. The alternative route is Cach Mang Thang Tam - Nguyen Thi Minh Khai - Huyen Tran Cong Chua - Thu Khoa Huan - Le Thanh Ton - Pham Hong Thai - Cach Mang Thang Tam. Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street will also become one-way over 1.5 km from Cao Thang to Huyen Tran Cong Chua. The alternative route is Truong Dinh - Vo Van Tan (or Nguyen Dinh Chieu) - Cao Thang - Nguyen Thi Minh Khai. Suong Nguyet Anh and Bui Thi Xuan streets near the Tao Dan Station will be opened to two-way traffic for all vehicles. The construction site at Bay Hien Station (ST7), located at the intersection of Cach Mang Thang Tam and Truong Chinh streets, will also be fenced off and occupy part of the roadway during the same period. Traffic on surrounding streets will be adjusted, with some sections converted to one-way traffic. At the Truong Chinh-Cach Mang Thang Tam-Ly Thuong Kiet-Hoang Van Thu intersection, vehicles will only be allowed to turn right onto Ly Thuong Kiet or left onto Hoang Van Thu, and will not be allowed to travel straight along Cach Mang Thang Tam. Vehicles traveling from Cach Mang Thang Tam toward the intersection must also turn right onto Hoang Van Thu. The Department of Construction said the traffic management plan is still provisional. The Management Board of Urban Railways, the project's investor, will determine and announce specific adjustment periods based on actual conditions at the construction sites. The affected streets are major routes connecting the city's northwestern gateways with central Ho Chi Minh City and carry heavy traffic. Relevant agencies will coordinate traffic diversions and regulation in phases to minimize disruptions to residents' travel and daily activities. Sections of Truong Chinh, Tan Ky Tan Quy and Huynh Van Gam streets will be fenced off from Sept. 16 to facilitate construction of ST9 (Ba Queo) Station. Traffic will continue as normal, but the city encourages people traveling from An Suong to central areas to use alternative routes to reduce congestion. One alternative route is Truong Chinh - Che Lan Vien - Nguyen Huu Dat - Le Trong Tan - Tan Ky Tan Quy - Truong Chinh. Another is Truong Chinh - Ho Dac Di - Huynh Van Gam - Tan Ky Tan Quy - Truong Chinh. Cars will be banned from traveling along Tan Ky Tan Quy Street in the Cong Hoa - Le Trong Tan direction. On Huynh Van Gam Street, cars will also be banned from traveling in the Tan Ky Tan Quy - Ho Dac Di direction. Cars had already been banned from traveling one way on Cach Mang Thang Tam Street, from Bay Hien Intersection to Dan Chu Roundabout, to serve construction of the Le Thi Rieng Station (ST5). Work on Metro Line 2 started in January this year. Costing more than VND55 trillion (US$2.12 billion), the 11.3-kmline will include 9.3 km of underground track, with 10 underground stations and one elevated station. The line is scheduled for completion in 2030, connecting central Ho Chi Minh City with its northwestern gateway.

picked.t: Southeast Asia's most populous metropolis ranks its 2nd smartest city
picked.body: In the inaugural Intelligent Cities Index 2026, released by global consulting firm Boston Consulting Group (BCG), the city state of Singapore ranked highest in Southeast Asia and 11th globally. It was followed by Jakarta, which ranked 39th worldwide. The Indonesian capital is the most populous city in Southeast Asia with 42 million people, according to an estimate by the U.N. Department of Economic and Social Affairs' Population Division in its World Urbanization Prospects 2025 report. The city even overtook Tokyo to become the world's most populous city last year, according to a United Nations study. Vietnam's most populous city, Ho Chi Minh, ranked 48th globally, making it the third smartest city in Southeast Asia, followed closely by Malaysia's capital, Kuala Lumpur, at 50th. No other Southeast Asian countries are ranked. The index evaluates how 61 major cities across 39 countries use artificial intelligence and digital technologies to serve residents and businesses across five areas: resident outcomes, intelligent city strategy, technology adoption, ways of working, and enabling factors such as infrastructure, talent and funding. The world's five leading cities are London, Dubai, New York City, Washington, D.C., and Amsterdam. BCG said the index shows that artificial intelligence is becoming a key foundation of intelligent cities. Cities with higher levels of AI adoption tend to have more use cases and deliver better outcomes for residents. Rather than focusing solely on technology infrastructure, the index examines how effectively cities turn digital capabilities into better services and quality of life. BCG said technology alone is not enough, with successful cities also requiring effective governance, funding, talent, infrastructure and innovation ecosystems. The report found that cities where residents use smart-city applications more frequently also tend to report higher satisfaction. London and Dubai, for example, combine high usage with strong satisfaction among app users. BCG also identified different paths for cities seeking to improve their intelligent-city maturity. Some succeed by developing balanced capabilities across multiple areas, while others focus on particular strengths such as strategy, governance, partnerships, infrastructure or talent. For cities seeking to advance, BCG recommends clarifying long-term priorities, improving governance and partnerships, expanding proven AI and digital services, and investing in data, technology, infrastructure and skills. The report said AI adoption can improve resident outcomes even in cities that have not yet developed world-class infrastructure or funding ecosystems. This suggests cities can begin by expanding practical AI-enabled services while building broader capabilities over time.

picked.t: 3 Vietnamese restaurants earn platinum status in global fine dining list
picked.body: The list indicates the growing international recognition of Vietnam's fine dining scene. Founded in 2016 as part of China's largest online travel platform Trip.com, Trip.Gourmet is a one-stop food guide, offering global restaurant rankings, travel-focused food content, and reservation options. This year's selection, published on Sept. 8, has 744 restaurants in 105 cities across 40 countries. Gia Located near Hanoi's historic Temple of Literature, Gia specializes in contemporary Vietnamese cuisine. The name originates from gia dinh , meaning family in Vietnamese. Gia tells the story of local flavors and childhood traditions, reinterpreting them through a refined, modern lens while using seasonal local ingredients and modern techniques. Hibana by KOKI Situated in the renowned 5 star luxury hotel Capella Hanoi, Hibana by KOKI offers an exclusive Japanese teppanyaki experience in an intimate 14-seat setting. The venue focuses on live cooking performances by skilled chefs using premium imported ingredients. Anan Saigon In Ho Chi Minh City, Anan Saigon, named after the phrase an an , meaning "eat, eat", is located in Cho Cu on Ton That Dam Street, a wet market in the heart of the city. In the words of the restaurant, the head chef elevates street food and traditional dishes into a fine dining experience using fresh local ingredients and incorporating French culinary techniques, all while retaining essential Vietnamese flavors. Its menu features signature creations such as the banh xeo taco, Da Lat street style pizza, Mekong Delta fish, broken rice, and fish sauce ice cream. According to the Michelin Guide, all three establishments earned their first Michelin star in June 2023. Since then, Gia, Hibana by KOKI, and Anan Saigon have successfully retained their one Michelin star every year, including the awards in June 2026.

picked.t: Vietnam's durian industry shifts from volume to value
picked.body: Vietnam’s durian industry has built concentrated production zones and gained global shelf space. Land, growers and business resources give it room to add value through preservation technology, deep processing, logistics and market expansion. The Central Highlands' Dak Lak Province, which accounts for about 22% of national durian-growing area, now has roughly 44,000 ha under the fruit, with nearly 30,000 ha in harvest. Its 2026 output is projected to hit a record of about 500,000 tonnes. But cold-chain infrastructure remains incomplete while post-harvest preservation and deep processing are limited. Production remains fragmented, value chain links are weak, and quality control and traceability lag growth. Former National Assembly Vice President Le Minh Hoan said the industry must move from a "commodity chain" to a "commodity ecosystem." That means involving farmers and buyers, plus cooperatives, input suppliers, exporters, banks, insurers, research institutes, universities, agricultural promotion agencies, logistics providers, quarantine authorities and consumers. Authorities should connect them, fostering long-term cooperation over seasonal buy-sell relationships. Standardization to boost competitiveness A comprehensive quality management and traceability system is a core requirement. It is also a priority of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment. Since July 1, 2026, the ministry’s agricultural product traceability system has been operational. To date, data on 48,754 products from nine product lines of 19 enterprises have been uploaded, while 24 of 34 cities and provinces have reported progress. Cumulatively, the system holds data on 158,234 products across 18,524 product lines, involving 200 companies and 2,948 households and cooperatives. The ministry has flagged durian as a priority commodity for chain-based traceability, linking growing-area codes, packing facilities, testing, quarantine and export consignments. It is finalizing data standards, APIs, connectivity procedures and interoperability with national systems, laying the groundwork for data to be created once and used many times. That matters for exports as international markets increasingly demand oversight of traceability, quality and food safety. Dak Lak aims to build durian ecosystem Dak Lak, a top producer, is shifting from expanding area to boosting quality and value. On Aug. 20, the General Administration of Customs of China approved 140 additional durian growing-area codes in Dak Lak covering more than 4,321 ha, along with 31 packing facilities with a combined area of over 91,000 square meters and capacity of about 5,470 tonnes per day. The approvals give the province more room to plug into formal export supply chains. Registered growing areas and packing facilities must fully comply with Vietnamese and importing-country rules, according to the ministry’s Department of Plant Production and Protection. Export consignments must be inspected for plant quarantine and food safety before shipping. Those requirements are critical to protecting Vietnamese durian quality and reputation. Dak Lak currently has around 41,000 hectares of durian, with this harvest expected to yield nearly 500,000 tonnes. In 2025, its durian export turnover was estimated at US$1.1 billion. However, newly approved growing area codes only cover about 17-28% of the province’s durian plantations, leaving plenty of room to expand production that meets export standards. At the local level, Dak Lak will not chase output at all costs. It is shifting from an "agricultural production" mindset to an "agricultural economy" approach, from merely selling products to building value chains and brands. The province will tighten control over growing areas and quality; foster links among businesses, cooperatives and producers; and encourage investment in deep processing, freezing, cold storage, packing centers and logistics. From the basalt-rich Central Highlands region to international markets, Vietnamese durian has a major opening to raise its value. Synchronizing raw-material areas, quality standards, traceability, processing and logistics will help the industry move from volume-driven growth to development based on quality, value and reputation. With support from ministries, local authorities, scientists, businesses and producers, Vietnam’s durian industry is building a stronger foundation to sharpen competitiveness and cement its place in global markets.

picked.t: Sanofi, VNVC sign joint declaration on next-generation vaccine manufacturing in Vietnam
picked.body: Sanofi Vietnam and VNVC signed a joint declaration on strategic cooperation in next-generation vaccine manufacturing in Vietnam at the Vietnam-France Business Forum in Paris on Sept. 10. The forum brought together businesses from the two countries, with the participation of Vietnam's Party General Secretary and President To Lam, French President Emmanuel Macron, and senior officials from both countries. Under the declaration, Sanofi and VNVC will work to strengthen Vietnam's domestic vaccine manufacturing capacity, increase supply autonomy, and address disease prevention needs. The cooperation also covers healthcare access, workforce development, and building a sustainable vaccine ecosystem. The companies are identifying vaccines for potential future production by VNVC, with three initially selected for further assessment. Following the signing, representatives of Vietnam's Ministry of Health, VNVC, and Sanofi visited Sanofi's manufacturing facility in Neuville-sur-Saône, France, to learn about its manufacturing technologies, expertise and quality systems and discuss the cooperation roadmap. The three vaccines identified as priorities are intended to address areas of high unmet demand and support disease prevention across different age groups, from infants and adolescents to adults and the elderly. VNVC plans to complete and put its Vaccine and Biologics Manufacturing Facility into operation by the end of 2027. The first vaccine batches are targeted for production in 2028, with vaccines manufactured in Vietnam expected to be commercialized from 2029. The partnership has developed through several stages, including a milestone during French President Emmanuel Macron's visit to Vietnam in 2025. The September 2026 declaration marks a further step, with the companies identifying specific product priorities and milestones for potential local vaccine manufacturing. Stephen Alix, Head of Vaccines, International at Sanofi, said the company supports Vietnam's efforts to advance science and technology, innovation and high-tech industries while strengthening its healthcare system. "With more than 70 years of presence in Vietnam, Sanofi deeply values the direction set by the Communist Party and Government of Vietnam in advancing science and technology, fostering innovation, developing high-tech industries, and strengthening the resilience of the national healthcare system," Alix said. "Through this initiative, Sanofi seeks to make a meaningful contribution to the country's goals and to the development of an increasingly advanced biotechnology ecosystem in Vietnam." Ngo Chi Dung, Chairman and General Director of VNVC, said the declaration marked a shift from outlining areas of cooperation toward implementing plans to localize next-generation vaccine manufacturing in Vietnam. VNVC's Vaccine and Biologics Manufacturing Facility in Tay Ninh has an initial investment of more than VND2.5 trillion (US$96.18 million) and covers over 26,000 square meters. The facility is designed to produce about 120 million vaccine doses a year and aims to meet international standards, including WHO-GMP, EU-GMP, and FDA-cGMP. VNVC said the project is intended to strengthen domestic capabilities in vaccine and biologics research, manufacturing and testing.

picked.t: ‘연준 금리인상’ 베트남 중앙銀, 달러환율 4거래일 연속 인상…’연일 사상 최고치’
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남의 기준환율이 또다시 사상 최고치를 경신했다. 미국 연방준비제도(Fed·연준)가 기준금리를 연 3.75~4%로 25bp 인상한 데 따른 영향이다. 17일 베트남중앙은행(SBV)은 기준환율을 달러당 2만5,632동으로 발표했다. 이는 전일 대비 6동 오른 것으로, 기준환율은 4거래일 연속 오르며 16일에 이어 또다시 사상 최고치를 경신했다. 중앙은행은 △은행 간 시장 환율 △주요 교역국 통화 가치 △거시경제 균형 및 정책 목표 등을 종합하여 기준 환율을 매일 고시한다. 베트남 각 은행은 기준 환율 기준 ±5% 변동 폭 내 마진을 붙여 달러를 사고 팔 수 있다. 베트남중앙은행은 지난 7월 중순 이후 은행권 공식 환율과 암시장 환율이 모두 약세를 보이는 가운데 기준환율을 지속적으로 인상하는 움직임을 보이고 있다. 기준환율이 인상되자 은행권 달러 환율도 상승세를 보였다. 비엣콤은행(Vietcombank)은 달러 환율을 매수 2만5,815동, 매도 2만6,225동으로 전일 종가 대비 45동 인상했고, 베트남투자개발은행(BIDV) 또한 2만5,805동, 2만6,185동으로 10동 올랐다. 테크콤은행은 2만5,816동, 2만6,197동으로 12동 상승했다. 호치민시의 일부 환전소 달러 매수·매도가는 각각 2만5,850동, 2만6,050동으로 소폭 상승했다. 다만 올해 초 강달러로 인해 암시장 환율이 2만8,000동을 넘어서던 것과 비교하면 여전히 낮은 수준이다. 중앙은행의 이번 금리 인상은 연준의 기준금리 인상에 기인했다. 한편 연준은 지난 16일(현지시간) 9월 연방공개시장위원회(FOMC)를 열고 기준금리를 연 3.75~4%로 0.25%포인트 인상했다. 연준의 금리 인상은 지난 2023년 7월 이후 3년여 만이다. FOMC 금리 인상 결정 이후 달러는 강세를 보였다. 주요 6개국 통화 대비 달러 가치를 나타내는 달러인덱스(DXY)는 약 100.34까지 상승하며 7주 만에 최고치를 기록했다.
